x: Thanks to some good last lap running by Blunden, Charlton and Stan Davies we eventually ran out winners of the "Dewar" Shield with a total of 141 points, with South London 145 and Herne Hill 177.
Positions: 2, Burfitt, 43.2; 7, Blowfield, 44.3; 10, Stimpson; 15, Heard; 20, Frost; 31, Charlton; 46, McDonald; 53, Shields; 83, Smith; 85, K.
Eddie Short ran the best of our men with Bill Lucas showing next best time and Steve Charlton and Tom Carter, despite a fall over a bicycle during his "leg," also ran well.
Stimpson, Kennedy, Popplewell, Bruce, Cuff, England, Bolam and Charlton. 2 miles walk.—A.
Bishop; 19, Popplewell; 20, Lewis; 23, Durrant; 24, Charlton; 25, L. Bishop; 26, McDonald, 28, Cuff; 29, England; 30, Gray; 33, Stace; 35, Chantler; 36, K.
Whitlock, of Walton, was first man home in 28.54 and our placings and times were: 6, Charlton, 29.49; 8, Brown, 29.56; 9, Davies, 29.59; 11, Towndrow, 30.24; 19, England, 31.48.

At the half-distance there was a group of four runners with Brown, Blowfield, Bill Lucas and Steve Charlton all nicely together in under the half-hour, which is good running for our five miles course.
Steve Charlton, who came into the team at the last moment owing to Len Herbert being indisposed, ran like a champion on the third stage and eventually handed over with a twenty-eight second lead.

The others followed at short intervals, Charlton 20th, Tobin 38th, Heard and Ken Stimpson 50th, MacDonald 60th and Housego 130th. The next time we saw them, which was about 5 miles, Ferguson had opened up a gap between Field and Thompson; our runners were round about the same as before.
